headline: Provisional experiment: executable meaning contracts across external-record and zero-knowledge representations.
claim_ceiling: None of the three candidates clears a defensible novelty gate. The recommendation is a bounded next experiment, not an established AGI opportunity or new vulnerability. Current prior art eliminates each broad headline.
method: Started with missing outcomes: reliable binding of private proofs to external facts, independent participation in visual collaborative work, and spontaneous communication despite severe motor constraints. Decomposed representation and interaction restrictions, then searched strongest visible competitors. Scores are judgments, not measured customer demand.

score_scale: 1 weak to 5 strong; uncertainty lowers the unresolved-gap score

candidates.name: External-record to ZK meaning-contract compiler
candidates.beneficiary: Developers and independent auditors of privacy-preserving identity and transaction applications.
candidates.missing_useful_outcome: A runnable certificate that external record identity, ranges, ordering and context survive client parsing, circuit encoding and verifier interpretation; counterexamples and a corrected adapter accompany failures.
candidates.binding_restriction: Separately implemented languages share field elements but not the intended external meaning. A circuit can compute its declared relation perfectly while an external uint256 or context is misrepresented.
candidates.strongest_competitor_and_gap: zkFuzz tests trace/constraint consistency and already handles substantially more than older underconstraint checkers [S1]. ZKProof explicitly identifies incompatible instance reductions [S2]; the 2026 ERC draft still specifies semantic context validation [S3]. These establish a real boundary, not proof no vendor serves it. Automatic cross-language contract extraction and certified repair were not established by this search.
candidates.constructed_mechanism: Require an explicit external meaning schema; have agents recover implementation mappings, synthesize inverse/injectivity and context-binding obligations, then emit deterministic checkers, minimized counterexamples and adapters. Unknown intended semantics must remain unknown.
candidates.enabling_change_and_connection: Hypothesis: capable code-reading agents can connect application schemas, serialization and circuit constraints into one executable boundary contract. The connection is between compiler representation correctness and cryptographic statement binding, rather than a new solver.
candidates.minimal_construction_and_falsifier: Ten public integrations, twenty hidden seeded ordering/range/context faults. Compare against zkFuzz plus an ordinary coding-agent baseline. Require at least 90% detection, at most 10% false alarms, and a threefold reduction in expert specification time. Reject if manual specification dominates or the baseline matches it. Thresholds are proposed, not results.
candidates.commercial_mechanism: Paid release checks and maintained integration adapters for security teams; no willingness-to-pay evidence gathered. Known checks must be cheaper to maintain than bespoke audits.
candidates.successor_inheritance: Versioned meaning schemas, small checked encoding kernels, negative examples and adapter-change obligations.
candidates.uncertainty: The automatically inferred/verified bridge was not built. Existing type systems, formal tools or audit products may already supply the residual. Code alone cannot reveal whether field equivalence or integer identity was intended.

candidates.name: Verified nonvisual editing of an existing canvas diagram
candidates.beneficiary: Blind engineers and analysts required to modify colleagues' existing diagrams in the originating application.
candidates.missing_useful_outcome: An exact native-format graph edit, with navigable semantic preview and a machine-checked account of changed nodes, edges and labels.
candidates.binding_restriction: The native canvas exposes neither sufficient semantic controls nor a complete keyboard authoring path; moving to a new authoring format can break team interoperability.
candidates.strongest_competitor_and_gap: Savant already offers natural-language application interaction [S6]. AccessFlow extracts graphs but specifies visual-editor verification [S7]; PreFigure already authors accessible mathematical diagrams [S8]. Diagramium explicitly lacks keyboard canvas editing and text exports for several diagram types [S9]. The residual is reliable editing and round-trip preservation in an existing unsupported format, not description or accessible authoring generally. Cross-application alternatives remain insufficiently searched.
candidates.constructed_mechanism: Infer an adapter from public application schemas/code; expose graph structure as screen-reader operations; translate requested edits into native mutations; verify a re-read graph against the requested semantic delta before saving.
candidates.enabling_change_and_connection: Agent-generated adapters connect accessibility interaction with bidirectional transformations and graph invariants. Pixels can suggest structure, but uncertain topology cannot become a silently accepted edit.
candidates.minimal_construction_and_falsifier: One public canvas format, twenty existing diagrams, three edit types. Require all intended graph changes and zero silent unintended edge/label changes, then evaluate independent use with blind participants. Reject if read/write access is absent, topology cannot be recovered reliably, or existing accessible tools already round-trip the required format.
candidates.commercial_mechanism: Employer accessibility procurement or vendor SDK; willingness to pay and adapter maintenance costs untested.
candidates.successor_inheritance: Native format adapters, graph edit invariants and accessible operation vocabulary.
candidates.uncertainty: A11yBoard and additional diagram-editing research require targeted review. A vendor-specific adapter could be ordinary accessibility implementation rather than a new capability.

candidates.name: Error-tolerant mixed-language AAC with targeted disambiguation
candidates.beneficiary: People using gaze or switch input whose spontaneous messages mix languages and contain input errors.
candidates.missing_useful_outcome: The user's exact intended utterance, recovered from noisy abbreviations with fewer costly selections, while preserving negation, names and language choice.
candidates.binding_restriction: Motor actions are expensive; typo correction and scanning long candidate lists can erase language-model prediction savings.
candidates.strongest_competitor_and_gap: SpeakFaster already expands abbreviations, uses context and offers repair paths. Its published prototype is English and its KeywordAE did not tolerate abbreviation typos [S10]. This is an explicit prototype limitation, not evidence that the entire 2026 AAC market lacks the capability. Generic ASR improvement was abandoned after current speaker-adaptation research [S11].
candidates.constructed_mechanism: Maintain a lattice of possible intended utterances conditioned on noisy input; ask the cheapest discriminating choice based on the user's motor costs; let the user confirm the final utterance. Preserve spelling fallback rather than forcing model suggestions.
candidates.enabling_change_and_connection: Combine multilingual language models, error-channel inference and active question selection. The proposed output is recovered intended text, not statistically plausible speech.
candidates.minimal_construction_and_falsifier: Public bilingual dialogue benchmark with explicitly synthetic gaze-error distributions, followed by user testing. Require lower total selection-plus-reading time than SpeakFaster-style expansion with ordinary correction; exact content and negation must match. Reject if candidate scanning or errors offset saved actions.
candidates.commercial_mechanism: License to AAC device/software vendors. Distribution, personalization and reimbursement economics are unvalidated.
candidates.successor_inheritance: User-controlled error models, multilingual ambiguity cases and measured interaction-cost policies.
candidates.uncertainty: No user data or trials. Synthetic errors cannot establish usability. Dasher and subsequent AAC products may anticipate the mechanism; novelty confidence is low.

sources.finding: Current circuit trace/constraint fuzzer; evaluation includes 452 Circom circuits.
Sections 3.6 and 3.7 explicitly discuss high-level semantics and incompatible instance reductions; age limits current-gap inference.
Semantic validation, ordered commitments, context binding and split 256-bit coordinates are already specified; not an adopted standard.
Bits2Num accumulation and strict variant are public prior art.
Diagram extraction, visual verification and accessible publication already offered.
Semantic accessible mathematical diagram authoring already available.
Incomplete keyboard authoring and exports explicitly acknowledged.
Abbreviation expansion and correction prior art; English/typo limitations reported.
Zero-shot dysarthric adaptation already studied; generic adaptation abandoned.
DOM agent excludes visual canvas and drawing; not the strongest multimodal competitor.
Diagram exploration already studied; mentions A11yBoard requiring follow-up.
Current public competing implementation exists; not executed.

retrieval_limits: Some PMC follow-up requests returned CAPTCHA; initial article retrieval and indexed original-paper excerpts were available.
Raw GitHub fetch disabled; GitHub rendered source was successfully read.
Circom operator documentation returned 502 twice; not treated as evidence.
ACM full text returned 403; indexed original-paper result used only for limited prior-art identification.
rejections: Generic circuit fuzzer: zkFuzz anticipates it.
Field aliases or two-limb repair as discovery: established circomlib and draft-spec mechanisms.
Code-only automatic intended-meaning inference: underdetermined without an external contract.
Diagram narration or accessible source authoring: AccessFlow, TADA and PreFigure anticipate it.
General natural-language screen reader: Savant anticipates it.
Generic dysarthric adaptation or LLM abbreviation expansion: existing research anticipates both.

probe_results.interpretation: Known class reproduced with controls. Strict field validation rejects legitimate values if the external requirement is all uint256; two limbs preserve them. Python transcription only: no Circom execution, new exploit, automatic bridge synthesis or competitor benchmark.

recommendation: Investigate E2-1 only through the stated comparative benchmark. If it merely automates established encoding checks, reject the discovery claim. Preserve E2-2 and E2-3 as lower-confidence alternatives; no production or commercial claim is justified.
